Basketball World Cup|2021 Latvia]]|[[United States men's national under-19 basketball team|Team]]}} }} '''Patrick O'Neal Baldwin Jr.''' (born November 18, 2002) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[KK Crvena zvezda|Crvena zvezda]] of the [[Basketball League of Serbia]] (KLS), the [[ABA League]], and the [[EuroLeague]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Milwaukee Panthers men's basketball|Milwaukee Panthers]]. He was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the top players in the 2021 class. ==Early life== Patrick Baldwin grew up in Evanston, Illinois until he was in 8th grade.{{cite web |last=Goldsmith |first=Charlie |date=February 9, 2020 |title=Men's Basketball: 'Something Special': High school phenom and Northwestern recruit Patrick Baldwin Jr. returns for homecoming game at Welsh-Ryan Arena |url=https://dailynorthwestern.com/2020/02/09/sports/mens-basketball-something-special-high-school-phenom-and-northwestern-recruit-patrick-baldwin-jr-returns-for-homecoming-game-at-welsh-ryan-arena |access-date=June 14, 2024 |work=The Daily Northwestern}} He was on several basketball teams including the league FAAM (Fellowship of Afro-American Men).{{cite web|title=FAAM turns 55: Decades of lessons in basketball and life|url=https://evanstonroundtable.com/2023/11/29/faam-evanston-youth-basketball-program/|website=EvanstonRoundtable.com|date=November 29, 2023|access-date=December 13, 2024}} In 2017, the summer before his freshman year, the Baldwin family moved to Wisconsin, because his father became the head men's basketball coach at the [[University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee]]. ==High school career== Baldwin played basketball for [[Sussex Hamilton High School|Hamilton High School]] in [[Sussex, Wisconsin]].{{cite web |last=Radcliffe |first=JR |date=November 26, 2017 |title=Top-flight freshman Patrick Baldwin Jr. is just part of the youth movement as Hamilton basketball starts season 2–0 |url=https://www.jsonline.com/story/communities/northwest/sports/2017/11/26/top-flight-freshman-patrick-baldwin-jr-just-part-youth-movement-hamilton-basketball-starts-season-2/896629001/ |access-date=April 11, 2021 |work=[[Milwaukee Journal Sentinel]]}} During his freshman year he was part of their 2017–18 team that made the state tournament, losing to future NBA All–Star [[Tyrese Haliburton]] and [[Oshkosh North High School|Oshkosh North]] 57–56 in the final.{{cite web|title=HHS Boys' Basketball 2017–18 Season|url=https://hamiltonchargers.sportngin.com/page/show/4170560-2017-18-season|website=HamiltonChargers.Sportngin.com|access-date=December 13, 2024|archive-date=May 21, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210521185026/https://hamiltonchargers.sportngin.com/page/show/4170560-2017-18-season|url-status=dead}} As a junior, Baldwin averaged 24.3 points and 10.8 rebounds per game, earning Wisconsin [[Gatorade Player of the Year awards|Gatorade Player of the Year]] honors.{{cite web|first=Jon|last=Masson|title=Sussex Hamilton's Patrick Baldwin Jr. earns Gatorade state player of the year honor for boys basketball|url=https://madison.com/wsj/sports/high-school/basketball/boys/sussex-hamiltons-patrick-baldwin-jr-earns-gatorade-state-player-of-the-year-honor-for-boys/article_ae4f0b83-ab0a-59c5-ac07-1d465c9308e0.html|work=[[Wisconsin State Journal]]|date=March 27, 2020|access-date=April 11, 2021}} During the second game of his senior season, Baldwin suffered a season-ending ankle injury.{{cite magazine |last=Jordan |first=Jason |date=December 14, 2020 |title=Sidelined with Season-Ending Injury, SI99 Wing Patrick Baldwin Jr. Focused on Recruitment |url=https://www.si.com/college/recruiting/basketball/patrick-baldwin-decision-looms-si99-duke-northwestern-uw-milwaukee-kentucky |access-date=April 11, 2021 |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]}} He was named to the rosters for the [[2021 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|McDonald's All-American Game]], [[Jordan Brand Classic]] and [[Nike Hoop Summit]].{{cite web |last=Hogg |first=Curt |date=February 23, 2021 |title=Two players from Wisconsin are named to the boys McDonald's All American Game |url=https://www.jsonline.com/story/sports/high-schools/2021/02/23/patrick-baldwin-jr-michael-foster-jr-named-mcdonalds-all-americans/4562887001/ |access-date=April 11, 2021 |work=[[Milwaukee Journal Sentinel]]}} ===Recruiting=== Baldwin was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the top players in the 2021 class. On May 12, 2021, he committed to playing college basketball for [[Milwaukee Panthers men's basketball|Milwaukee]] under the coaching of his father over offers from [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]], [[Arizona State]], [[Iowa]], [[Kansas]], [[Kentucky]], [[LSU]], [[Michigan]], [[North Carolina]], [[University of Southern California|USC]] and [[Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball|Georgetown]]. He was also the youngest person ever to receive an offer to play at [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]], receiving the offer in his sophomore year of high school.{{cite magazine|first=Jason|last=Jordan|title=Elite Prep Wing Patrick Baldwin Jr. Commits to UW-Milwaukee|url=https://www.si.com/college/recruiting/basketball/patrick-baldwin-commits-uw-milwaukee|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|date=May 12, 2021|access-date=May 12, 2021}} He became the highest-rated recruit to ever commit to a [[Horizon League]] program.{{cite web |last1=Givony |first1=Jonathan |last2=Biancardi |first2=Paul |author-link2=Paul Biancardi |name-list-style=and |date=May 12, 2021 |title=Five-star college basketball recruit Patrick Baldwin to play for father at Milwaukee |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/31432017 |access-date=May 12, 2021 }} ==College career== In his college debut, Baldwin posted 21 points and 10 rebounds in a 75–60 win against [[2021–22 North Dakota Fighting Hawks men's basketball team|North Dakota]].{{cite news |date=November 10, 2021 |title=Baldwin's double-double leads Milwaukee past North Dakota |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401365588 |access-date=November 15, 2021 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]]}} On November 23, 2021, he suffered a leg injury in a loss to [[2021–22 Bowling Green Falcons men's basketball team|Bowling Green]], forcing him to miss several games.{{cite news |last=Rosiak |first=Todd |date=November 23, 2021 |title=Bowling Green 82, UWM 68: Patrick Baldwin Jr. misses most of the second half with leg injury |url=https://www.jsonline.com/story/sports/college/uwm/2021/11/23/bowling-green-82-uw-milwaukee-68-patrick-baldwin-jr-injured/8731006002/ |access-date=November 29, 2021 |work=[[Milwaukee Journal-Sentinel]]}} Baldwin suffered an ankle injury on January 5, 2022, in a 63–49 win against [[2021–22 Green Bay Phoenix men's basketball team|Green Bay]].{{cite news |last=Rosiak |first=Todd |date=January 5, 2022 |title=UWM 63, UWGB 49: Panthers smother Phoenix for second straight win, but Patrick Baldwin Jr. is hurt again |url=https://www.jsonline.com/story/sports/college/uwm/2022/01/05/uw-milwaukee-63-uw-green-bay-49-panthers-defense-key-victory/9101640002/ |access-date=January 25, 2022 |work=[[Milwaukee Journal-Sentinel]]}} Baldwin returned on February 4, 2022, in a 70–60 loss to [[2021–22 Purdue Fort Wayne Mastodons men's basketball team|Purdue Fort Wayne]], where he shot 5-of-15, and 1-of-6 from 3. He also played the next two conference games against [[2021–22 Cleveland State Vikings men's basketball team|Cleveland State]] and [[2021–22 Northern Kentucky Norse men's basketball team|Northern Kentucky]], averaging 30 minutes and 6.5 points while shooting 4-of-19 overall (1-of-11 from 3), before sitting out the rest of the season for undisclosed reasons. Baldwin averaged 12.1 points and 5.8 rebounds per game as a freshman in an injury-plagued season. On April 22, 2022, Baldwin declared for the [[2022 NBA draft]], forgoing his remaining college eligibility.{{cite web |date=April 22, 2022 |title=Patrick Baldwin Jr. entering NBA draft after injury-marred season at Milwaukee |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/33784271 |access-date=April 22, 2022 |website=ESPN.com}} ==Professional career== ===Golden State / Santa Cruz Warriors (2022–2023)=== Baldwin was selected with the 28th overall pick by the [[Golden State Warriors]] in the [[2022 NBA draft]].{{cite web |date=June 23, 2022 |title=Warriors Select Patrick Baldwin Jr. (#28) & Gui Santos (#55) in 2022 NBA Draft, Presented by Oracle |url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors-draft-results-20220623 |access-date=June 23, 2022 |website=NBA.com}} On July 6, 2022, the Warriors announced that they had signed Baldwin.{{cite web |date=July 6, 2022 |title=Warriors Sign 2022 First Round Draft Pick Patrick Baldwin Jr. |url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors-sign-patrick-baldwin-jr-20220706 |access-date=July 6, 2022 |website=NBA.com}} Baldwin was assigned to the Golden State [[G League]] affiliate, the [[Santa Cruz Warriors]], on October 24, 2022.{{cite tweet|author=Warriors PR|title=Warriors assign Patrick Baldwin Jr. and Ryan Rollins to Santa Cruz|number=1584414136024244224|user=WarriorsPR|date=October 23, 2022|access-date=October 23, 2022}} He then made his NBA debut on October 30 in a 128–114 loss to the Detroit Pistons,{{cite web|title=Patrick Baldwin Jr. 2022-23 Game Log|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4433246/type/nba/year/2023|website=ESPN.com|access-date=October 19, 2023}} playing only in the final minute of the game. On December 21, 2022, Baldwin scored a career high of 17 points in a 143–113 blowout loss to the [[2022–23 Brooklyn Nets season|Brooklyn Nets]], shooting 6-of-10 overall and 5-of-8 from three in 23 minutes of play.{{cite web|title=Golden State Warriors vs. Brooklyn Nets Live Score and Stats - December 21, 2022 Gametracker|url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/gametracker/boxscore/NBA_20221221_GS@BKN/|website=CBSSports.com|access-date=December 29, 2022}} This performance was followed by an 11-point showing in a 112–107 victory over the [[2022–23 Utah Jazz season|Utah Jazz]] a week later, shooting 4-of-7 overall and 3-of-5 from three in just 13 minutes.{{cite web|title=Utah Jazz vs Golden State Warriors - December 28, 2022|url=https://www.foxsports.com/nba/utah-jazz-vs-golden-state-warriors-dec-28-2022-game-boxscore-39661|website=FOXSports.com|access-date=December 29, 2022}} Baldwin was assigned to the G League again on February 5, 2023.{{cite web |last=Stinar |first=Ben |date=February 5, 2023 |title=Golden State Warriors Make A Roster Move On Sunday |url=https://www.si.com/fannation/nba/fastbreak/.amp/news/patrick-baldwin-jr-roster-move-golden-state-warriors-news-sunday |access-date=February 11, 2023 |website=SI.com}} ===Washington Wizards / Capital City Go-Go (2023–2025)=== On July 6, 2023, the Warriors traded Baldwin, [[Jordan Poole]], [[Ryan Rollins]] and draft picks to the [[Washington Wizards]] in exchange for [[Chris Paul]].{{cite web|title=Wizards acquire Poole, Baldwin Jr. and Rollins along with a First and Second Round Pick in trade with Warriors|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/news/wizards-acquire-poole-baldwin-jr-and-rollins-along-with-a-first-and-second-round-pick-in-trade-with-warriors|website=NBA.com|date=July 6, 2023|access-date=July 6, 2023}} Throughout his first two seasons with the Wizards, he had been [[NBA G League#Standard assignment|assigned]] several times to the [[Capital City Go-Go]].{{cite web|title=2023-2024 Capital City Go-Go Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/teams/Capital-City-Go-Go/55/Transaction_History/2024|website=RealGM.com|access-date=January 4, 2025}}{{cite web |title=2024-2025 Capital City Go-Go Transaction History |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/teams/Capital-City-Go-Go/55/Transaction_History/2025 |access-date=January 4, 2025 |website=RealGM.com}} On February 6, 2025, Baldwin was traded to the [[San Antonio Spurs]] in a multi-team trade,{{cite web |date=February 6, 2025 |title=Wizards Acquire Middleton, Johnson From Milwaukee Bucks |url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/news/wizards-acquire-middleton-johnson-from-milwaukee-bucks |access-date=April 13, 2025 |work=NBA.com |quote=As part of a four-team deal, the Wizards also acquired the draft rights to Mathias Lessort from the New York Knicks and dealt Patrick Baldwin Jr. to San Antonio.}} but was waived the next day.{{Cite web |last=Stinar |first=Ben |date=2025-02-07 |title=San Antonio Spurs Release Former NBA 1st-Round Pick After Wizards Trade |url=https://www.si.com/fannation/nba/fastbreak/san-antonio-spurs-release-former-nba-1st-round-pick-after-wizards-trade-baldwin-jr |access-date=2025-02-08 |website=Fastbreak On SI |language=en-US}} ===San Diego / Los Angeles Clippers (2025–2026)=== On February 19, 2025, Baldwin signed with the [[San Diego Clippers (NBA G League)|San Diego Clippers]] of the [[NBA G League]],{{Cite web |date=2025-02-19 |title=Recently Traded Bucks Player Signs With New Team |url=https://www.si.com/nba/clippers/news/recently-traded-bucks-player-patrick-baldwin-clippers |access-date=2025-03-01 |website=Los Angeles Clippers On SI |language=en-US}} and on March 1, he signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].{{Cite web |last=Kiemen |first=Joe |date=2025-03-01 |title=Patrick Baldwin Jr. Signs with Clippers on March 01, 2025 {{!}} Knup Sports |url=https://knupsports.com/patrick-baldwin-jr-signs-with-clippers-on-march-01-2025/ |access-date=2025-03-01 |website=knupsports.com}} Baldwin made two appearances for Los Angeles, averaging 3.0 points, 1.5 rebounds, and 0.5 assists. On July 29, Baldwin was waived by the Clippers.{{cite web | last=Veazey | first=Austin | title=Ex-Warriors First-Round Pick Waived by LA Clippers | website=Golden State Warriors On SI | date=2025-07-29 | url=https://www.si.com/nba/warriors/onsi/news/ex-warriors-first-round-pick-waived-by-la-clippers-01k1c1z1m8xe | access-date=2025-12-09}} On October 2, the Clippers signed Baldwin Jr. to a training camp contract. He was waived prior to the start of the regular season on October 18.{{Cite web |title=Clippers officially waive 6-foot-9 ex-Warriors forward, G-League superstar guard |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/article/clippers-officially-waive-6-foot-143002955.html |access-date=October 24, 2025 |website=Yahoo! Sports |language=en}} On January 16, 2026, Baldwin signed a 10-day contract with Los Angeles.{{Cite web|title=LA Clippers Sign Patrick Baldwin Jr. To 10-Day Contract|url=https://gleague.nba.com/news/la-clippers-sign-patrick-baldwin-jr-to-10-day-contract|access-date=January 20, 2026|website=gleague.nba.com|language=en}} In two games for the Clippers, he averaged 5.0 points and 0.5 rebounds. ===Philadelphia 76ers (2026)=== On February 5, 2026, Baldwin signed a 10-day contract with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].{{Cite web |last=Grimm |first=Harrison |date=2026-02-05 |title=Sixers reportedly sign Patrick Baldwin Jr. to 10-day contract |url=https://www.libertyballers.com/76ers-news/85850/sixers-reportedly-sign-patrick-baldwin-jr-to-10-day-contract |access-date=2026-02-06 |website=Liberty Ballers |language=en-US}} He made one appearance for the 76ers, recording no points and one rebound. Following the expiration of his 10-day contract, Baldwin returned to the [[San Diego Clippers]]. ===Sacramento Kings (2026)=== On February 22, 2026, Baldwin signed a two-way contract with the [[Sacramento Kings]].{{Cite web|title=Kings Sign Patrick Baldwin Jr. To Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-sign-patrick-baldwin-jr-to-two-way-contract|access-date=February 23, 2026|website=nba.com|language=en}} === Crvena zvezda Meridianbet (2026–present) === On July 18, 2026, Baldwin signed with [[KK Crvena zvezda|Crvena zvezda]] of the [[Basketball League of Serbia]] (KLS), the [[ABA League]], and the [[EuroLeague]].{{Cite web |date=2026-07-18 |title=Patrik Boldvin junior novo pojačanje Crvene zvezde Meridianbet! {{!}} KK Crvena zvezda |url=https://kkcrvenazvezda.rs/news/patrik-boldvin-junior-novo-pojacanje-crvene-zvezde |access-date=2026-07-18 |website=kkcrvenazvezda.rs |language=sr}} ==National team career== Baldwin represented the [[United States men's national under-19 basketball team|United States]] at the [[2021 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup|2021 FIBA Under-19 World Cup]] in Latvia. He averaged 7.7 points and five rebounds per game, helping the team win the gold medal.{{cite web |title=Patrick Baldwin Jr (USA)'s profile – FIBA U19 Basketball World Cup 2021 |url=http://www.fiba.basketball/world/u19/2021/player/Patrick-Baldwin-Jr |access-date=July 12, 2021 |website=FIBA.basketball |publisher=[[FIBA]]}} He shot 47 percent from the floor, helping the team win the gold medal.
